# Web Security Gotchas

> Framework-agnostic browser and HTTP security-header patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors. These reproduce on any stack -- Hono, Express, Fastify, Next.js, Go, Rails -- because the behaviour lives in the browser and the specs, not in your router.

## Entries

- [`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` also nulls `Origin` on form POSTs, so an Origin-based CSRF guard refuses your own site](referrer-policy-nulls-origin-on-form-post.md): Two individually-correct hardenings that kill every write path when shipped together -- under `no-referrer`, Fetch sends `Origin: null` on a navigational POST, and an Origin-matching CSRF guard refuses it. GETs keep working so the app looks alive, `curl` cannot reproduce it, and tests that set `Origin` by hand never see it. Check `Sec-Fetch-Site` first (forbidden header, immune to referrer policy) and move to `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`. HIGH.
- [CSP belongs to the response, not the template: a page rendered by one layout and served with another route's header map silently loses its own stylesheet and scripts](csp-header-map-mismatch-blocks-own-assets.md): Once an app has more than one header map (signed-out vs. authenticated vs. embedded), the template and the headers are independent choices and nothing ties them together -- so a route returns byte-perfect HTML in an envelope whose CSP forbids the assets that HTML references. Missing `style-src 'self'` renders the page as unstyled default-serif HTML; a `script-src` hash sitting in a map the route never sends makes a button silently dead; `script-src` without `connect-src` lets the script run and refuses its fetch. The response is 200, the asset URL is 200, only one route is affected, the sole error is in the user's console, and tests that check the header map and the rendered markup separately are both green. Bind headers to the layout, and test by pairing each response's rendered `<link>`/`<script>` against that same response's own CSP. HIGH.
